name: Folk
blurb: Front-porch folk: boom-chick steel-string guitar, an alternating root-five upright bass, and a modal fiddle air over a brushed stomp-and-tambourine pulse.

flavors.label: Front Porch Ballad
flavors.blurb: Slow and sung: two open chords, long ringing strums, nobody in a hurry.

flavors.label: Old Time Breakdown
flavors.blurb: Fiddle-tune drive - hard boom-chick, plain triads, the tempo the dancers set.

flavors.label: Modal Drone
flavors.blurb: One chord in a modal banjo tuning, the way a sawmill-tuned fiddle tune just sits there and turns.

flavors.label: Parlor Rag
flavors.blurb: Fingerpicked ragtime folk: dominant sevenths walking round the circle, bouncy and precise.

flavors.label: Murder Ballad
flavors.blurb: Minor and grim - the aeolian fall to bVI, brushed and heavy, told rather than danced.

arranger.llmStyleBrief: Folk harmony is plain triads - no jazz stacks; the colour comes from open strings and drones. Major tunes are strophic I-IV-V. Modal tunes avoid the major V entirely, leaning on i-bVII double tonic, dorian i-IV, or the aeolian i-bVII-bVI fall. Harmonic rhythm is slow, two bars a chord. Ragtime parlor tunes are the one place dominant sevenths belong.
